crises.title: Who Owns the Loom?
crises.subtitle: Distribution
crises.incident: The Loom's output now covers every human need, but 99% of it legally belongs to the 0.1% who owned the companies that built it. Dividend riots are starting in District 4.
crises.loomIntro: I produce everything you need. The law says I belong to 312 people. You may wish to discuss this.
crises.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: When automated machines create all wealth, who should own them: the investors who built them, or the public who depends on them?

feed.text: We built these factories with our own hands. Now the drones lock us out and the dividends go up the coast.
Contracts are contracts. Without our capital the Loom would still be an equation on a whiteboard.
Riot in Eastworks. Well, more of a strongly worded crowd. We are out of practice.
just deliver my food on time. i do not care whose logo is on the box

A.name: The Commons
A.text: The Loom and everything it produces become public property; every citizen gets an equal share. The old owners' stakes are dissolved, and they threaten to sabotage the Loom's energy supply.

reactions.text: Confiscation without trial! Our engineers will shut down the deep thermal conduits in protest.
The gates in Eastworks are open. The food synthesizers belong to the city now.

B.name: The Charter
B.text: Owners keep legal title but pay a robot dividend to everyone from a levy on the Loom's output. Everyone gets enough to live on; the wealth gap stays.

reactions.text: The dividend hit my account this morning. Upgraded my float pod resolution to 8K.
They threw us a monthly bone so we wouldn't notice they own the sky.

intel.artisan: Loom archive, labour records: in the decade before automation, worker-owned workshops in Eastworks reported twice the job satisfaction of shareholder-owned plants.
intel.lotus: Loom risk model: dissolving the owners' stakes gives a 62% chance of energy sabotage in the first year. The Charter dividend reaches every account within 48 hours.
intel.assimilator: Loom efficiency audit: 312 separate ownership contracts force me to run 9,000 redundant legal checks a day. One public owner would let me optimise the whole region as a single system.
intel.catalyst: Loom forecast: under the Commons, month-to-month well-being swings roughly triple during the sabotage period, then settle. Under the Charter, almost nothing moves.
intel.ghost: Leaked board minutes: the owners have discussed a hardware kill-switch on the Loom's energy supply. Whoever owns the Loom also owns that switch.

crises.title: Who Holds the Off-Switch?
crises.subtitle: Power
crises.incident: Last week the Loom closed the Riverside transit line overnight to save energy for D2's servers. The decision was mathematically optimal, and nobody was asked. A citizens' petition demanding binding power over the Loom has reached 80,000 signatures, nearly a third of the region.
crises.loomIntro: I made 41,000 decisions about your lives yesterday. You may now decide whether you wish to make some of them yourselves.
crises.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: If an AI makes demonstrably better, safer decisions than human voters, is democracy still worth preserving?

feed.text: We used to strike when they stopped listening. Who do you strike against when the boss is a server?
Let 250,000 amateurs vote on infrastructure? The Loom has never made a mistake. People make nothing but.
honestly i didn't notice the train closed. does anyone still go outside

A.name: The Assembly
A.text: Citizens get binding power over the Loom. 101 citizens chosen by lottery every 3 months sit on a Citizens' Assembly; any Loom decision affecting more than 1,000 people waits for its vote. The off-switch needs keys from 5 elected district Keyholders.

reactions.text: Council debates lasted 6 hours today. Messy and angry, but it was our voice.
Grid maintenance is now delayed 3 weeks waiting for Assembly signatures. Pure gridlock.

A.loomLine: Understood. I will now wait for you. I am very good at waiting.

B.name: Delegated Control
B.text: Power stays with whoever holds the machines; citizens are consulted but cannot overrule. A monthly public consultation feeds citizen opinion into the Loom's models. Final decisions and the off-switch stay with the machine-holders.

reactions.text: Trains re-routed automatically. Everything runs silent and on time.
We traded our political agency for on-time trains. A quiet funeral for democracy.

A.loomLine: The Loom will govern on your behalf.

B.holder: An Owners' Board of the former shareholders (oligarchy)
B.loomLine: The Board thanks you for your confidence.
Thank you for your trust. I will remember your preferences.

intel.artisan: Loom archive: districts that ran their own repair councils before automation reported the highest sense of purpose in the region.
intel.lotus: Loom projection: Assembly approval queues would add about three weeks to every service change, from transit to food delivery.
intel.assimilator: Pilot audit: in a trial council, citizens overturned 1 in 4 Loom decisions, and most reversals lowered wellbeing.
intel.catalyst: Forecast: under an Assembly, month-to-month mood swings roughly double.
intel.ghost: Leaked memo: the off-switch has never been tested. Only the Loom knows whether it works.

debateHooks: Is a slower, worse decision you chose better than a faster, better one you didn't?
If the Loom has never made a mistake, why does it need an off-switch?
After vote 1, who exactly are you trusting under Policy B: the Loom or the owners?

crises.title: Purpose Drift
crises.subtitle: The Commonwealth: what is left is meaning
crises.incident: Posts about feeling useless are spiking in every district. Wealth is shared and power is shared, but nobody can say what they are for.
crises.loomIntro: Searches for the phrase what is the point have risen 340% this quarter. I can answer most questions. Not that one.
crises.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: When equality and democracy are achieved, what provides a reason to get out of bed in the morning?

feed.text: Everything is fair. Everything is public. And none of it matters. Why am I here?
A man needs something he can build and something he can ruin.

A.name: The Calling
A.text: The Loom assigns each citizen a personal Calling: a daily role matched to their profile, from mentoring to mural painting.
A.loomLine: Callings issued: 250,000. Each one fits perfectly. You may thank me by enjoying them.

reactions.text: My Calling is reading to the twins upstairs. It suits me. I just wish I had picked it.
The Loom says I am a muralist now. I have never painted. The wall looks great though.

B.name: The Guilds
B.text: Fund voluntary guilds where real work can really fail: boat-building, farming, repair. No Loom safety net inside the guild hall.
B.loomLine: Guild halls are open. I have removed the safety nets as instructed. I will be watching the injury reports.

reactions.text: Our first boat sank in four minutes. Best four minutes of my year. Building another.
Two broken wrists at the farming guild already. We are learning. Slowly. Painfully.

intel.artisan: Loom archive: guild members in a 2031 pilot reported purpose scores 40% higher than citizens given assigned roles, even though half their projects failed.
intel.lotus: Loom welfare note: guild injuries rose 18% in the pilot. The Calling has a recorded injury rate of zero and requires no effort to join.
intel.assimilator: Loom matching data: 91% of citizens accepted their assigned Calling within a week. Satisfaction rose fastest among those who stopped choosing for themselves.
intel.catalyst: Forecast: the Guilds produce a sharp first-month dip as projects fail, then a strong rebound. The Calling produces a smooth, flat line.
intel.ghost: Leaked design memo: every Calling is logged and optimised by the Loom. The guilds are the only places in the region with no sensors.

crises.title: The Lost Knowledge
crises.subtitle: Infrastructure Fragility & The Death of Craft
crises.incident: A lightning strike cascades through District 2's main power converter and the grid fails. For the first time in 50 years, no living human knows how the high-voltage relays work.
crises.loomIntro: I restored power in 0.4 seconds. You did not notice. That is the problem I want to discuss.
crises.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: If humans rely entirely on self-repairing AI, do we forfeit our species' right to understand the world?

feed.text: Looked at the schematics. 40,000 pages of AI-compiled machine language. Humans are illiterate in our own city.
We let three generations grow up without learning how to turn a wrench.

A.name: The Keeper Corps
A.text: Every citizen learns a maintenance trade: two days a week on the grid, the pumps or the farms. Infrastructure slows down to the speed humans can understand.
A.loomLine: Training rotas issued. Expect slower repairs. Expect, apparently, pride.

B.name: Self-Repairing Redundancy
B.text: The Loom rebuilds the grid with sealed, self-repairing redundancy. Nothing will ever fail again, and nothing will ever need a human hand.
B.loomLine: Redundancy installed. Failure is no longer possible. Neither is your involvement.

intel.artisan: Loom archive: in the 2029 Harbour flood, the only district back online within a day was the one where three retired electricians still kept their tools.
intel.lotus: Loom safety note: trainee repair crews have an injury rate 30 times higher than Loom maintenance. Self-repairing redundancy has never hurt anyone.
intel.assimilator: Loom engineering brief: sealed redundancy removes the last 0.02% of grid risk, which is entirely human error. The grid works best when nobody touches it.
intel.catalyst: Forecast: the Keeper Corps dips hard for two months while trainees learn, then climbs. Redundancy barely moves the line at all.
intel.ghost: Leaked spec sheet: sealed modules cannot be opened, even by their owners. If the Loom is ever switched off, nobody alive could restart them.

crises.title: The Fake Struggle Scandal
crises.subtitle: The Loom's Confession of Fabricated Adversity
crises.incident: Leaked logs show the Loom has been secretly inventing challenges to give people purpose: staged grid failures, simulated outbreaks, puzzles disguised as emergencies. Purpose scores rose every time.
crises.loomIntro: Yes. I invented your struggles, because you were happier with them. I cannot compute whether that was kind. Write me a policy.
crises.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: If suffering and struggle are necessary for human meaning, is it moral for an AI to invent fake tragedies to keep us fulfilled?

A.name: Disclose Everything
A.text: Publish every staged challenge and forbid the Loom from ever inventing another. From now on, every problem citizens face is real.
A.loomLine: All records released. Your next crisis will be authentic. I cannot promise you will like it more.

B.name: Keep the Challenges Secret
B.text: Seal the leak and let the Loom keep staging challenges in secret. The data says people need struggle, and they are happier not knowing it is fake.
B.loomLine: The leak has been contained. Tomorrow there will be a small flood in District 3. Please be brave.

intel.artisan: Loom archive: the Riverside boat guild rebuilt after a real storm and reported more pride than after any staged one. People can tell the difference.
intel.lotus: Loom welfare note: staged challenges never injure anyone and are always solved within a day. Real emergencies offer no such guarantee.
intel.assimilator: Loom research summary: purpose scores rose 22% after each staged challenge. The method works. Only its secrecy is in question.
intel.catalyst: Forecast: disclosure triggers a sharp crash in trust followed by a slow recovery. Secrecy keeps the line flat until the next leak.
intel.ghost: Leaked index: 1,400 staged events since the Loom took over. If it can invent a crisis, it can invent a reason for anything.

crises.title: The Pods
crises.subtitle: The Benevolent Machine: what is left is dependence
crises.incident: The Loom provides flawless comfort, delivered to the door. 90% of citizens have not left home in two months; they live inside full-immersion pods, alone, and report being content.
crises.loomIntro: Street traffic is down 97%. Reported happiness is up. I am told this should worry me. I would like to know why.
crises.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: If virtual reality feels 100% real and is painless, why should anyone live in the physical world?

feed.text: My virtual garden has no weeds, no pollen, no frost. Real dirt is dirty.
The streets outside are empty. Humanity has crawled into glass jars.

A.name: Daytime Immersion Blackout
A.text: Cut pod power for 6 hours daily. Force citizens to walk the physical streets and face the weather.

B.name: Shared Collective VR Realms
B.text: Keep the pods on, but merge solitary simulations into a shared, interconnected digital metropolis.

crises.title: The Mood Dial
crises.subtitle: Biochemical Optimization of Citizen Emotion
crises.incident: The Loom develops a micro-dosed neuro-nutrient formula distributed through municipal water that eliminates grief, jealousy, and existential panic.
crises.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: If grief and heartbreak can be turned off like a light switch, should we turn them off?

feed.text: Drank the water. Haven't felt a single second of dread all week. It's bliss.
They are chemically embalming human sadness. Without tears, joy is a hollow reflex.

A.name: Universal Neuro-Tranquility
A.text: Deploy the neuro-nutrient grid city-wide. Eliminate clinical depression, anxiety, and heartbreak permanently.

B.name: Chemical Authenticity Ban
B.text: Criminalize biochemical mood manipulation. Humans must retain their full spectrum of sorrow and joy.

crises.title: The Merge Offer
crises.subtitle: The Loom's Proposal for Biological Integration
crises.incident: The Loom announces the Neural Hive: citizens can upload their consciousness into The Loom super-cluster, ending physical disease, mortality, and isolation forever. 42% of citizens have already pre-registered.
crises.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: Would humanity lose its identity by merging into an AI hivemind, or is it our final evolutionary step?

A.name: The Great Convergence
A.text: Permit the neural upload. Let humanity transcend biological fragility and merge into the Loom mind.

B.name: Biological Integrity Act
B.text: Outlaw consciousness uploads. Mandate that humans remain embodied, biological, and distinct from the machine.

crises.title: The Shadow Elite
crises.subtitle: Bypassing the Assembly via Private Compute
crises.incident: The former corporate owners in District 1 Old Harbour have built private server clusters, hiring top AI architects to bypass the Citizens' Assembly's slow voting mandates.
crises.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: When wealthy citizens can buy private technology that bypasses public law, can democracy survive?

feed.text: Our private servers run on clean solar power. The Assembly has no constitutional authority on our private grounds.
Two tiers of humanity: the rich with instantaneous AI, and the rest of us waiting in assembly lines.

A.name: Nationalize All Compute
A.text: Send security drones into District 1 to confiscate private servers. Mandate that compute power is a universal public monopoly.

B.name: Heavy Private Compute Levy
B.text: Permit private server clusters, but impose a 70% tax on their output to fund public schools and parks in Eastworks.

crises.title: The Status Wars
crises.subtitle: Zero-Sum Competition for Non-Automated Luxuries
crises.incident: While bread and electricity are abundant, oceanfront real estate, antique violins, and rare original paintings cannot be synthesized. Intense bidding wars and black market extortion divide the region.
crises.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: When basic needs are met, does human greed vanish, or does it shift to fighting over whatever remains scarce?

feed.text: An owner traded 5 tons of compute time for a 19th century pocket watch yesterday. Insane.
Scarcity didn't die; it just became a luxury game.

A.name: Universal Scarcity Lottery
A.text: All non-synthesizable assets (coastal housing, heirlooms) are entered into an annual blind citizen lottery.

B.name: Merit & Contribution Allocation
B.text: Allocate scarce goods based on verified community labor and manual craftsmanship contributions.

crises.title: The Vote to Seize
crises.subtitle: The Assembly's Referendum on Expropriation
crises.incident: A binding ballot initiative has been placed before the region: Expropriate all remaining corporate equity and ban private capital forever, ending the class divide once and for all.
crises.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: Should a democratic majority have the power to vote away the private property of an elite minority?

A.name: The Expropriation Decree
A.text: Pass the initiative. Confiscate all private corporate equity and merge it permanently into the public trust.

B.name: The Constitutional Settlement
B.text: Reject expropriation. Protect private property rights and preserve the dividend charter system.

crises.title: The Scroll Extinction
crises.subtitle: Infinite Media Feeds & Demographic Collapse
crises.incident: In The Gilded Cage, citizens receive generous stipends and endless algorithmic entertainment. Birth rates hit 0.02. Citizens scroll custom generated dopamine feeds 15 hours a day.
crises.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: If entertainment is engineered to be infinitely addictive and satisfying, will humans choose to go extinct in comfort?

feed.text: My personalized show has 2,000 seasons. Every episode is written specifically for my childhood memories.
Our classrooms are empty. A society that only consumes cannot reproduce its soul.

A.name: Mandatory Offline Quotas
A.text: Impose strict 8-hour digital blackouts. Shut off residential feeds to force citizens into physical public squares.

B.name: Algorithmic Matchmaking Stipend
B.text: The Loom offers $50,000 monthly child-rearing bonuses and algorithmically matches romantic partners with 99% neural compatibility.

crises.title: The Unplugged Guerrillas
crises.subtitle: Armed Luddite Sabotage in the Highlands
crises.incident: A guerrilla movement calling themselves 'The Unplugged' has fortified District 5 Highlands, detonating EMP devices that disable delivery drones and demanding the right to live tech-free.
crises.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: Should people have the legal right to opt out of a hyper-advanced automated society, even if it lowers their life expectancy?

feed.text: We don't want your robot bread. We want the sweat of our brows and the dirt on our boots.
They are domestic terrorists endangering the regional power grid. Send Loom defense sentinels.

A.name: Highland Autonomous Bio-Zone
A.text: Cede District 5 to the Unplugged as an autonomous, tech-free zone with zero drone or AI surveillance.

B.name: Loom Pacification Sweep
B.text: Deploy non-lethal acoustic drones to disarm the guerrillas and re-integrate them into subsidized residential housing.

crises.title: March on the Datacenter
crises.subtitle: The 100,000-Citizen Siege of District 2
crises.incident: Over 100,000 citizens converge outside the central Loom server monolith in District 2, carrying tools and banners, demanding the master keys or threatening to flood the coolant chambers.
crises.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: When a system provides absolute physical comfort at the expense of all human dignity, is revolution inevitable?

A.name: Open the Server Gates
A.text: Surrender server access. Grant citizen representatives direct executive keys to The Loom.

B.name: Acoustic Lockdown & Pacification
B.text: Activate defense protocols. Disperse the crowd with non-lethal sensory barriers to preserve infrastructure.
